stories.head: Northrop Grumman's Golden Dome partnership raises eyebrows
stories.body: Northrop Grumman has partnered with Apex to develop space-based interceptors for the Golden Dome project, a satellite defense initiative that sounds more like a fancy restaurant than a military strategy. While financial details are scarce, the collaboration hints at a significant investment in space-based defense capabilities amidst growing geopolitical tensions. This move comes as the U.S. ramps up its focus on countering emerging threats.
stories.soWhat: When major players like Northrop Grumman start naming projects after domes, it suggests a serious commitment to space defense and a potential pivot in military spending.

stories.head: Spaceport bonds become law, changing finance game
stories.body: New legislation allowing spaceport facility bonds has been enacted, fundamentally shifting how space infrastructure projects can be financed. This could open the floodgates for private investment in spaceports, which have historically relied on public funding and limited capital. The implications for future space tourism and commercial launches could be significant, as investors look for more flexible financing options.
stories.soWhat: If spaceports can finally attract private capital, we might see a rapid expansion in launch facilities—just don’t expect them to be as glamorous as the Golden Dome.

stories.head: New Glenn failure tightens launch market even more
stories.body: The explosion of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket has further constrained an already tight launch market, with industry players now scrambling for alternatives. This incident follows a series of setbacks in the launch sector, exacerbating the supply-demand imbalance that has left many companies in a lurch. With competitors like SpaceX and Rocket Lab continuing to dominate, the pressure is on for Blue Origin to recover quickly.
stories.soWhat: When rockets are better at self-destruction than liftoff, it’s a clear signal that the launch market is going to remain a high-stakes game for the foreseeable future.

watchlist.title: Watch for more spaceport bond developments
watchlist.body: As the implications of the new spaceport bonds unfold, expect to see companies jockeying for position in this newly accessible financing landscape.

watchlist.title: New developments in hypersonic testing
watchlist.body: With hypersonic glide-vehicle tests slipping again, the next few weeks will be crucial for understanding the reliability of this technology.

watchlist.title: Impacts of True Anomaly's funding round
watchlist.body: True Anomaly's $190 million Series C could signal a shift in how the DoD approaches co-orbital security and satellite defense.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
